questions.q: In whom does David take refuge?
questions.a: David takes refuge in Yahweh his God.

questions.q: What is David asking Yahweh to do?
questions.a: David is asking Yahweh to save him from those who chase him, and to rescue him.

questions.q: What does David say should happen to him if he has done wrong?
questions.a: David says that if he has done wrong, his enemy should be allowed to chase and capture him and leave him lying dead.

questions.q: What is David asking Yahweh to do in Yahweh’s anger?
questions.a: David is asking Yahweh show that he is greater than what David’s furious enemies can do.

questions.q: What does David say Yahweh has already ordered?
questions.a: David says that Yahweh has already ordered judgment.

questions.q: What does David want Yahweh to do concerning the peoples?
questions.a: David wants Yahweh to take his rightful place ruling over all the peoples.

questions.q: Who does David want Yahweh to judge?
questions.a: David wants Yahweh to judge all the peoples, including himself.

questions.q: What does David say the righteous God does?
questions.a: David says God examines thoughts and desires.

questions.q: Where does David’s protection come from?

questions.a: God saves the upright in heart.
David describes God as a righteous judge who is indignant each day.

questions.q: What will God do if a person does not repent?
questions.a: God will sharpen his sword and will prepare his bow for battle.

questions.q: How does David describe the wicked person who does not repent?
questions.a: David describes the wicked person as filled with evil intentions, as though pregnant with them, and as one who lies as naturally as giving birth.

questions.q: What happens to the wicked man who digs a pit?
questions.a: He falls into the hole he has made.

questions.q: What happens to the trouble and violence of the wicked man?
questions.a: He experiences the bad and violent things that he wants to do to others.

questions.q: For what will David give thanks to Yahweh?
questions.a: David will give thanks to Yahweh for his righteousness.

questions.q: To whom will David sing praise?
questions.a: David will sing praise to the name of Yahweh, the Most High.

commentary.text: The psalmist prays to God to plead his cause, and judge for him.
He expresses confidence in God, and will give him the glory of his deliverance.

Verses 1–9 David flees to God for succour. But Christ alone could call on Heaven to attest his uprightness in all things. All His works were wrought in righteousness; and the prince of this world found nothing whereof justly to accuse him. Yet for our sakes, submitting to be charged as guilty, he suffered all evils, but, being innocent, he triumphed over them all. The plea is, “For the righteous God trieth the hearts and the reins.” He knows the secret wickedness of the wicked, and how to bring it to an end; he is witness to the secret sincerity of the just, and has ways of establishing it. When a man has made peace with God about all his sins, upon the terms of grace and mercy, through the sacrifice of the Mediator, he may, in comparison with his enemies, appeal to God's justice to decide.

David is confident that he shall find God his powerful Saviour. The destruction of sinners may be prevented by their conversion; for it is threatened, If he turn not from his evil way, let him expect it will be his ruin. But amidst the threatenings of wrath, we have a gracious offer of mercy. God gives sinners warning of their danger, and space to repent, and prevent it. He is slow to punish, and long-suffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish. The sinner is described, ver. #(14–16), as taking more pains to ruin his soul than, if directed aright, would save it. This is true, in a sense, of all sinners. Let us look to the Saviour under all our trials. Blessed Lord, give us grace to look to thee in the path of tribulation, going before thy church and people, and marking the way by thine own spotless example. Under all the persecutions which in our lesser trials mark our way, let the looking to Jesus animate our minds and comfort our hearts.
